Now, where does conflict between profile build_requires and recipe build_requires happen? In extend_build_requires — build_requires from recipe and profile are combined into one list; each processed in a loop; they both belong to same node "node" so `previous = node.public_deps.get(name, context)`. entries.author: teacher
entries.content: Root cause: when a lockfile legitimately contains the same build_requires package in two different contexts (e.g. `tool/1.0` in the host context coming from the recipe via `build_requires(..., force_host_context=True)` and `tool/2.0` in the build context coming from the profile), `GraphLock.lock_node()` matched locked build_requires **by package name only**. The name-keyed dict collapsed both entries, so when installing with the lockfile, both the host-context and build-context requirements were locked to the same node (the last one in the dict), installing the wrong version for one of them. Fix: in `conans/model/graph_lock.py`, build_requires are now matched by `(name, context)` using the locked node's context and the requirement's `build_require_context`; a requirement whose context isn't locked now raises "Build-require '<name>' cannot be found in lockfile" instead of silently locking to the wrong context. Verified with the reproduction scenario plus the full graph_lock, build_requires, cross_building and graph integration test suites.
